summary: Embedding payload contains trailing padding tokens causing sporadic rerank score inflation and elevated latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent rerank responses where a small subset of results receive unexpectedly high similarity scores and end-to-end rerank latency spikes to 1.5–2x normal. Responses are 200 OK but rank order and scores are inconsistent with local offline similarity checks.

Impact:
- Affects ScribeAI production traffic to rerank endpoint for search+recommend flows (dedicated pool).
- ~0.8% of requests in the last 24h show inflated top-1 scores and median latency increase from 120ms -> 240ms for rerank stage.
- Causes downstream UX regressions for end users (wrong top result) and increased token/compute costs.

Environment:
- Dedicated customer cluster in us-east using redwood-embed-large-v2 for embeddings and rerank-lite-v1 for reranker.
- Running on Dedicated capacity with autoscaling disabled.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Submit batch of 32 candidate embeddings (shape 32x1536) with query embedding produced by the same client library.
2. Call /v1/rerank with embed payloads passing content-type: application/json and custom header X-Embed-Version: 2.
3. Observe returned scores; intermittent high score for irrelevant candidate and rerank stage latency spike.

Observed behavior:
- 200 OK, but one candidate has cosine similarity near 0.999 while offline cosine between the same vectors is ~0.72.
- Rerank stage duration spikes in logs (see attached snippets).
- No 5xx errors reported.

Expected behavior:
- Scores should match offline similarity calculations within expected numeric tolerance (~1e-3 after normalization).

Initial logs / request snippets:
- Customer provided encoded JSON payload; analysis shows some embedding vectors include trailing zeros and a few include repeated small-magnitude padding values (1e-38).
- Server access logs: request id req-20260305-8f4e includes rerank duration 245ms; dependency logs show embeddings-service decode time 150ms for that request.

Notes:
- Customer upgraded client SDK last week. They report the issue started after the SDK change.
- They are on dedicated plan; entitlement allows priority support.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-05: Support intake from CS (Asha). Customer sent sample payload and server request_id.

2026-03-05: Replayed sample request in staging: noticed embedding decoding in embeddings-service takes 3x longer when payload contains trailing small-magnitude values (potential float32/float16 decode path trigger).

2026-03-06: Hypothesis A: Client SDK switched to a compact binary-encoded JSON that our decoder treats as generic float -> triggers fallback parsing that pads vectors to next 64-byte boundary, leaving garbage values in tail elements.

2026-03-06: Hypothesis B: Some vectors labeled as length 1536 are being transmitted with header length 1536 but payload truncated to 1532 and server fills remaining dims with uninitialized stack memory (low-probability), leading to extreme similarity matches due to accidental near-identical tails between candidates.

2026-03-06: Ran synthetic A/B in staging: sending intentionally padded trailing 1e-38 floats reproduced both the inflated similarity and a 2x decode time increase in embeddings-service. This strongly points to a decoder path that falls back to a slower normalization routine when input contains denormal/subnormal values.

2026-03-06: Cross-linked with backend team: PR reference github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2784 touches embedding-decoder fast-paths; suspect change interacts badly with new client binary format.
2026-03-07: Reached out to ScribeAI engineer (customer contact) for SDK version and example of raw bytes; they confirmed upgrade from 1.4.2 -> 1.5.0 coincides with issue onset.
comments: Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-05: Logged initial ticket after customer provided sample request_id and payload. Assigned to Marco for deeper debug.

Marco Diaz (Eng) 2026-03-06: Reproduced locally with customer payload. Observed trailing denormals causing code path switch in embeddings-service. Opening investigation; added serving-runtime and embeddings-service owners to thread (#infra-embed).

Nora Klein (SRE) 2026-03-06: Captured pprof of embeddings-service during problematic decode; allocation spike observed. Attaching flamegraph link to ticket. Recommend rate-limiting this customer's batch size while we triage to reduce cost impact.
Customer (ScribeAI - dev@scribeai.com) 2026-03-06: Confirmed SDK version change; offered to roll back if that helps. Also provided base64 of raw payload for offline analysis.

Marco Diaz (Eng) 2026-03-07: Temporary mitigation: server side validation will detect subnormal values and run a fast sanitizer to clamp denormals to 0.0 before normalization. Deploying canary to us-east for this customer for immediate relief.
resolution: (in progress) Applied a canary sanitizer on embeddings-service in us-east that clamps subnormal values to 0.0 and logs occurrences. Early canary results show eliminated score inflation and rerank latency returned to baseline for the sampled requests. Awaiting customer confirmation and planning a follow-up: 1) coordinate with SDK team to produce a compatibility patch, 2) harden decoder fast-paths and expand unit tests to include denormal/compact-encoding cases, 3) create post-incident doc and update embedding payload validation guidance in the SDK docs.
follow_up_actions: Coordinate with SDK team to release client patch (ScribeAI indicated willingness to test).
Add regression tests for denormal/padded vectors to embeddings-service CI.
Create Internal runbook entry describing sanitizer and when to enable for other customers.
